result.summary:
Validated lib/letflow/design/iss0923-catalog-delete-blocks-on-pinned-instances.md against real code (read-only; no mix run needed, no lib/test edits, no mutants). VERIFIED CORRECT: delete/1 at service_catalog.ex:880-895 gates only on referencing_active_definitions (:940-950; query :960-969 filters status == :active); @service_task_reference_fragment :952-958 takes (graph column, service_id) and is reusable; delete_entry/1 :904-911 rescues Ecto.StaleEntryError; InstanceProjection.terminal?/1 instance_projection.ex:223-225 is true for :completed/:cancelled only, false for :active/:error (stored as 'ACTIVE'/'ERROR' via Ecto.Enum :139); projection PK instance_id :136, InstanceDefinitionSnapshot PK instance_id + graph :map at instance_definition_snapshot.ex:93-98; idx_proj_status is partial `where: "status = 'ACTIVE'"` (migration 20260816120003:49-53); service_catalog_versions has no FK, unique index (service_id, version) idx_service_catalog_versions_service_id_version (migration 20260921000004:84-93); caller set of ServiceCatalog.delete/1 in lib/ is only routers/admin_services.ex:275 and its case (:275-287) has no catch-all so the new router clause is genuinely mandatory; Error.service_referenced_by_active_definitions/1 at error.ex:428-437 and the proposed sibling shape are consistent; Version rows are read only inside service_catalog.ex (publish/resolve paths), so deleting them cannot break a third module; the re-register collision argument is real (do_publish archive_current_version would hit the surviving (service_id,version) unique row); existing concurrent-delete test (service_catalog_test.exs:427-453) stays valid with versions-first-then-entry inside a transaction because the locker holds a lock only on the entry row; snapshots are created for every instance including sub-process children (engine.ex:1319, engine/sub_process.ex:366) so the snapshot-graph proxy covers child instances; no web/src or OpenAPI consumer of the 409 types (grep). Security reasoning (INV-1/2/5/6/7/8) is sound and INV-9 correctly not applicable. No implementation code present. Every ISS-0923 requirement (decide block vs document) is covered, and AC-1..AC-14 map to design elements, signatures and error shape are fully specified.

FAIL REASON (one load-bearing factual error, per the no-partial-credit rule): Section 6 (D-E, TOCTOU) justifies 'no lock' with: 'a row lock on the public service_catalog entry would not be taken by Engine.create/2 (which does not read the entry at start; resolution happens later through resolve_pinned_version/3)'. This is FALSE against the code. Engine.create/2 DOES read the live service_catalog row at instance start: engine.ex:1278-1281 `pin_lookup/2` defaults to `PinLookup.build()`, whose catalog_lookup/1 (service_catalog/pin_lookup.ex:63-73) does `Repo.get(Entry, service_id)` and returns not_found for a missing row and for a RETIRED row; PinLookup's own moduledoc (:16-20) says it is the START-time lookup. So the real race has two sides the design never describes: (a) create reads the entry before delete commits and guard 3 runs before the new snapshot/projection are committed -> instance pinned to a deleted service (the case the design describes); (b) delete commits first -> Engine.create fails at start with a pin-lookup not_found, not an ERROR instance, so the design's stated outcome 'that instance goes to ERROR ... exactly today's behaviour' is only half right. Because the premise is wrong, the claim that closing the window 'would require the engine to take a shared lock on the catalog row at start ... engine change' and the cost reasoning are unverified rather than defensible: the engine already does a plain Repo.get on that row at start, so the real cost/shape of a FOR SHARE / retire-first fix is different from what D-E says. The decision (accept, document, advise retire first) may still be right, and the retire advice is actually well founded (RETIRED makes PinLookup refuse new starts), but the design must state the true mechanism before REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER and ELIXIR-DEV build the @doc text (section 9(e)) and the OQ list on it.
issues: BLOCKER (design section 6, D-E): false claim that Engine.create/2 does not read the service_catalog entry at start. Real code: engine.ex:1278-1281 + service_catalog/pin_lookup.ex:63-73 (Repo.get(Entry, service_id); :RETIRED and missing -> {:error, :not_found}). Rewrite the TOCTOU analysis from the real mechanism: name both interleavings (create-before-delete -> pinned instance on a deleted service; delete-before-create -> create rejects at start, no instance), state precisely what a fix would need (PinLookup/Engine plain read today, no lock), and re-justify accept/no-lock on that basis. Also make section 9(e)'s @doc wording consistent (retire is the sound closure because PinLookup refuses RETIRED at start).

MINOR (AC-6): cites test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs ~:471 as an existing delete assertion; :471 is the update_scope narrowing test (describe AC7). The delete assertion is only :384 (plus :396, :412 success cases and the concurrent test :427-453). Correct the line references.

MINOR (section 3.1 / 2.1): claims determinism ('ids ascending within a tenant', 'collected tenant by tenant in list_registrations/0 order') but TenantProvisioning.list_registrations/0 is `Repo.all(Registration)` with no ORDER BY (tenant_provisioning.ex:274-276), so tenant order and therefore WHICH 50 ids are returned when truncated is not stable across calls. Either say tenant order is unspecified (and tests must not assert it) or specify a sort of registrations.

MINOR (section 7): says the unique index idx_service_catalog_versions_service_id_version is 'on the entry side'; the index is on service_catalog_versions (migration 20260921000004:91-93), Entry only references it via unique_constraint. Reword.

TEST-DESIGNER should not depend on an unmade implementation choice; fix the seam (direct insert of minimal instance_projections + instance_definition_snapshots rows into the tenant schema works without any production accessor).
